traps.title: Repeat use is falling in every segment, even though the total is rising
traps.explanation: The blended repeat-plan rate rises from about 25% to about 29%, but filter by segment: existing cardholders fall from about 40% to 33%, and new-to-credit customers from about 19% to 14%. The total rises only because the mix shifted toward existing cardholders, who repeat more. Engagement is getting worse, not better.

traps.title: Early plans per user were a launch spike
traps.explanation: Plans per active user started near 2.0 in week 1 and settled at about 1.15 by week 5. The launch weeks reflect curiosity and promotion. Judge engagement on the steady-state weeks, not on a comparison with week 1.

traps.title: Purchases bunch just below the $500 fee threshold
traps.explanation: About three times as many purchases fall between $450 and $499.99 as between $500 and $549.99. Purchase sizes do not naturally drop off a cliff at $500; customers are keeping purchases under the threshold to avoid the $25 Flex 4 Plus fee. The product rule is shaping behavior, which matters for any fee or pricing decision.
